description: The time column. Its presence makes the table a time-series table.
name: time-column

description: Comma-separated columns that identify a series.
name: series-key

description: Partition size: how much time one partition covers.
name: chunk-interval

default.derived: true with a series key, else false

description: Rows with the same (series, time) count once; the latest write wins. Applied within an append, by the Timelake reader, and by compaction. Fixed at creation: files written with it off may hold copies, which the reader would then miss.
name: dedup

description: The column holding each row's insertion time (`ingest_time=False` or `--no-ingest-time` leaves it out). Each append fills it with the time the append started, unless the input brings its own values. Among rows with the same (series, time), the latest insertion wins, then the later commit.
name: ingest-time-column

description: Maintenance drops partitions that end before now minus this duration, e.g. 90d.
name: retention

description: Run size-tiered compaction, retention, and snapshot expiry inline after appends. One append can override it (`maintain=` in Python, `--no-maintain` on the CLI).
name: auto-maintain

description: Inline compaction merges a size tier of a partition once it has this many files.
name: compact-min-files

description: Inline maintenance rewrites a partition whole (sorted, duplicates removed) once the table holds data newer than the partition's end by this much and the partition has two small files, whether the append touched it or not. `off` leaves it to the size tiers.
name: compact-cold-after

description: The Timelake reader returns only the latest write of each (series, time), before compaction has removed the older copies. Has no effect on tables with dedup off.
name: read-dedup

description: How the reader removes copies: `merge` merges the files that may share keys in key order; `keys-first` lists the older copies from the key columns, then reads the files like any scan and leaves them out (slower on the industrial IoT benchmark).
name: read-dedup-strategy

description: Size at which compaction output and writes roll to a new file (256 MiB).
name: target-file-size-bytes

description: Parquet row group size. Page indexes keep single-series reads selective inside large row groups.
name: row-group-rows

description: Expire snapshots older than this, keeping at least `min-snapshots` and at most `max-snapshots`.
name: snapshot-retention

description: Snapshots always kept, whatever their age.
name: min-snapshots

description: Snapshots kept at most: older ones expire even if younger than `snapshot-retention`.
name: max-snapshots

description: Format of the head object (`metadata/timelake-head`): `arrow`, `json`, a registered codec, or `none` for no head.
name: head-format

description: Room in the head for the last-value index, then the Parquet footers of the newest files (1 MiB). What doesn't fit is read separately.
name: head-inline-bytes

description: No snapshot expires before this time. `timelake upgrade` sets it so the upgrade can be rolled back.
name: keep-snapshots-until

default.derived: the current format for new tables; 0.1.0 if absent

description: The table format. Timelake refuses tables of a newer format it can't handle; `timelake upgrade` brings a table to the current format.
name: format-version
